name: StickyBar
summary: A bar of controls that sticks within its section: the first child of a section (or any block), it sticks under the site header (`--dl-chrome-block`, which SiteLayout measures) once its own place scrolls away, only while its parent is on screen, and leaves with it. Stuck, it takes the floating material and a raised shadow (`data-stuck`); at rest it has no fill or shadow, and its geometry never changes between the two. Not for the page's own header (SiteLayout's header already sticks), for a toolbar that floats over a canvas (use FloatingBar) or for a bar that should stay for the whole page (put it in the header). Added for DesignUp's Talks finder (LR4, 2026-11-12): "Search and filters bar: this should be a sticky header within the section when it scrolls out of view."
a11y: No role of its own: its controls carry their names (a search field, a select). A control that takes focus while under the stuck bar (Tab moves past it to its section's content) is scrolled clear of it, so focus is never hidden (WCAG 2.4.11). Its parent's scroll container decides where it sticks: the window under SiteLayout, or a scrolling region it sits in.

props.name: children
props.description: The bar's controls: a search field, filters, a sort, a count.

props.name: bleed
props.description: Inside SiteLayout: the bar reaches into the page margin (`--c-site-layout-margin`) on both sides and pads back by the same amount, so its controls stay on the column at rest and, stuck, it reads as one strip under the header.

settings.description: Above and below the bar's controls, at rest and stuck alike (default space.stack-item).
